sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the southern edge of Moorestown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. South Church Street runs the full height of the sheet from top to bottom, with South Washington Avenue parallel to it on the right and Sutton Avenue and Cooper Avenue crossing both. The blocks between South Church Street and South Washington Avenue (numbered 186 and 187) are lined with frame dwellings and their outbuildings; the largest building is a garage with show room and capacity for 80 cars near the top of block 89, beside a small boiler room, with frame bleachers shown dotted to its north. West of South Church Street the land is divided into long narrow lots running off the sheet edge, each with a dwelling, and a store, a co-op building and a small pump house are lettered there. Block 188 east of South Washington Avenue is mostly open ground with a few dwellings at its top. At the bottom, Hooten's Creek crosses the sheet under a concrete bridge at South Church Street, and a lake with an island fills the lower right. The left and right margins and the bottom edge are marked No Exposure. A compass rose stands at the left. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run down South Church Street and South Washington Avenue and along Cooper Avenue, and the scale bar is at the lower left. The neighbouring sheets are 3 above, 14 to the left and 191 and 188 to the right.
notes: Streets are today's South Church Street, South Washington Avenue, West Sutton Avenue and West Cooper Avenue.
Four junctions only; the fit has no leave-one-out value and rests on the four street crossings.
South end: S. Church St, S. Washington Av, Sutton Av, Cooper Av, Hooten's Creek and lake at the bottom. 50 ft. Upright (north upper right). 4 junctions only.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the residential south side of Moorestown below West Prospect Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. South Church Street runs down the left of the sheet and South Washington Avenue down the right; West Prospect Avenue crosses the top and Harris Avenue crosses two thirds of the way down. The left-hand strip is a single row of deep lots facing South Church Street, with frame dwellings and their outbuildings and a short Private Drive leading west to a cluster of sheds and automobile houses; beyond the rear lot lines the sheet is marked No Exposure. Between South Church Street and South Washington Avenue lies block 88, divided into house lots with dwellings along both streets and a lumber and truck storage building with a wood drying shed in its middle. East of South Washington Avenue a row of dwellings faces the street in block 87, and below Harris Avenue block 89 is mostly undeveloped apart from a few houses along South Washington Avenue. A boxed inset at the bottom right, with its own north arrow and labelled 3, shows the rear of part of block 87 with a storage building, a shed and an outbuilding; it is not drawn in its ground position on the sheet. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run in the streets; the streets are marked 50 and 60 feet wide.
notes: Harris Avenue is West Harris Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The boxed inset of block 87 at the bottom right has no street junction and was left out of the georeferenced part (cut out of the mask).
S. Church St, W. Prospect Av, S. Washington Av, Harris Av. 50 ft. Part 2: boxed inset at bottom right (block 87/89 continuation, own north arrow), no street junction.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: boxed inset at bottom right: rear of part of block 87 with storage building and shed (no street junction; drawn out of position with its own north arrow; needs a placed neighbour drawing the same buildings (none in this atlas)).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows West Main Street west of the centre of Moorestown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. West Main runs down the middle of the sheet, bending slightly, with West 2nd Street parallel to it along the left side. Union Street crosses at the top and Locust at about two thirds of the way down, and Camden Avenue leaves West Main at the lower left on a slant. Between West 2nd Street and West Main the blocks (27 and 69) hold frame dwellings and automobile houses, and several lots carry a co-op or stable. West of West Main the blocks are narrow strips running off to the right and are mostly frame dwellings, with a veterinary hospital, a furniture upholstery shop and a horn shop among them, and a few pink brick dwellings. The right half of the sheet is open ground behind long lots and is marked No Exposure along its right edge. A fire alarm box stands at Locust and West Main. Water pipes of 4, 8 and 10 inches run in the streets. The compass rose is at the right. Neighbouring sheets are 9 above the left, 8 to the left, 5 above, 14 to the right and 21 below.
notes: West Main also appears on this sheet as the street continuing north-east into sheet 5; the modern name is West Main Street.
Camden Avenue is not used as a control junction because it leaves West Main on a slant and its junction was not measured.
W. Main St with W. 2nd, Union, Locust, Camden Av. 50 ft. Turned (north upper left). 4 junctions only.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the centre of Moorestown around the crossing of West Main Street and Church Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the left. West Main Street runs down the middle of the sheet and West 2nd Street along its left edge; North Church Street and South Church Street cross both near mid-height, Tippenhauser Avenue runs along the top of the first block, Union Street along the bottom, and West Prospect Avenue and the end of South Washington Avenue fill the right-hand side. The blocks along West Main Street are the commercial core: a row of stores, a post office and further stores at the corner of North Church Street, and on the opposite block a garage for 25 cars with an auto repair shop, the Hose Co. No. 1 fire house and the fire department. Trinity P.E. Church with its parish house, chapel, vestry and rectory stands on a cemetery lot at West 2nd and North Church Street, and the M.P. Church is further down West Main Street. On the far side of Main Street are Our Lady of Good Counsel R.C. Church and School with its rectory, convent and a parochial school, and John O'Donnell's wagon shop and auto body builders with its sawing, upholstering and paint rooms and a lumber shed. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with outbuildings on deep lots. The lower right quarter is largely open ground behind the South Church Street lots. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets.
notes: Tippenhauser Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.
The street lettered W. Washington Av. at the top left corner is today's North Washington Avenue.
Centre: W. Main St, N./S. Church St, W. 2nd St, Union St, W. Prospect Av, Tippenhauser Av. 50 ft. Turned: north to the left (rotation about -59).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the centre of Moorestown east of the crossing of Main and Church streets, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. East Main runs down the middle of the sheet, changing to West Main at Mill, with East 2nd Street and West 2nd Street along the left side and High and the end of West Prospect Avenue on the right. Mill runs across at about two thirds of the way down, and Tippenhauser Avenue closes the bottom. On East Main the blocks hold stores and offices, among them the Moorestown Trust Co., a hotel, a moving picture house with lobby, bake house, drug store, plumbing shop and a lodge room, with the 1st Baptist Church lower down on West Main. On the right of East Main stand the Town Hall with cells, a home for aged, and the Community House with its gymnasium; below High there are frame dwellings, a filling station and a number of small dwellings and churches. The left side of the sheet is built up with frame dwellings, including a row of semi-detached houses on East 2nd Street. A compass rose is at the upper right and the right margin is marked No Exposure. Neighbouring sheets are 7 above, 5 to the left, 10 below the left, 3 below the right.
notes: French Av is today's Frenchs Avenue.
Tippenhauser Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.
The street lettered N. Washington Av. at the lower left corner is today's North Washington Avenue.
East 2nd Street and Frenchs Avenue is a hand-picked control point; the French Av junction is drawn narrow at the sheet edge and was not detected.
E./W. Main at Mill, E./W. 2nd, High, Prospect, French Av, Town Hall, Community House. 50 ft. Turned. East 2nd / Frenchs Av hand-picked.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the Friends' property on East Main in the east of Moorestown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. East Main crosses from the lower middle to the top, with Chester Avenue across the upper left, Schooley along the top edge, and East 2nd Street at the left; Page Lane runs off East Main to the right below the middle. A large part of the left side is Friends' Cemetery, with a tool house, and below it a row of buildings on East Main including the Burlington County Trust Co. bank, an American Soda Products Co. fertilizer packing and wax modelling works, auto repairing, a drug store, lodge rooms and the Moorestown M.E. Church. On the right are the Moorestown Friends' School buildings (class rooms, chapel, kindergarten) and a long auto and storage shed, and in the lower right the Moorestown Friends' High School with its auditorium, drawn from plans. Upper left blocks hold frame dwellings, a tin shop and Evans Apartments. The strip at the left edge is the margin of sheet 12. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are marked. The right edge is marked No Exposure. Neighbouring sheets are 24 above, 18 and 16 across the top, 6 below, 19 to the right.
notes: Snyder Av is today's Snyder Place, Page Lane is Pages Lane and Schooley is Schooley Street.
East 2nd Street jogs about 25 m at Chester Avenue; OpenStreetMap has two Chester Avenue and East 2nd Street nodes for it, and both were accepted.
The fit uses five points, two of them from single drawn edges, and has a high leave-one-out error.
E. Main at Chester Av, Friends' cemetery and schools, Page Lane, Schooley, Snyder Av. 50 ft. Turned. E. 2nd St jogs about 25 m at Chester Av; poorly controlled.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the area west of the centre of Moorestown between West 2nd Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. West 3rd Street runs down the left of the sheet and West 2nd Street down the right, with Locust crossing both about three fifths of the way down and Mannion Avenue closing the bottom. West Central Avenue runs along the upper left beside the Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division tracks, and Kenilworth Avenue enters at the lower left corner. The blocks between West 3rd and West 2nd Streets (60) are filled with frame dwellings and outbuildings on regular lots, a furniture upholstery shop and a few co-op buildings; the block south of Locust (68) is mostly open with dwellings facing Mannion Avenue. The triangle between West Central Avenue and West 3rd Street (61) has a few frame dwellings on lots that narrow toward the railroad. The lower left (62) is largely open. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches run in the streets and fire hydrants are marked. The compass is at the upper left. Neighbouring sheets are 9 above, 4 to the right, 16 to the left, 15 below the left and 21 below.
notes: Mannion Avenue, Kenilworth Avenue and Locust are today's Mannion Avenue, Kenilworth Avenue and Locust Street.
The Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division at the top left is the line OpenStreetMap calls Pemberton Industrial Track.
W. 3rd and W. 2nd with Locust, Mannion Av, Kenilworth Av, W. Central Av. 50 ft. Turned. 4 junctions only.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the West Moorestown railroad district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. The Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division crosses from the lower left to the top, with the West Moorestown passenger station and a freight station beside it; West Central Avenue and North Church run beside the line and Dawson crosses the top left. West 3rd Street and West 2nd Street run down the right of the line, with North Washington Avenue along the top and Union along the bottom. The largest buildings are the Moorestown High School, built 1914 and drawn with an auditorium, lunch room and manual training rooms, and Moorestown Public School No. 9 with its gymnasium and class rooms, both on block 10. In the lower middle are the C. A. Lippincott & Bro. Inc. contractors and farm implements works, with warehouse, oil and fertilizer store, a coal pile and sidings, and an auto repair shop. The blocks along West 3rd and West 2nd Streets are dwellings, small stores and a plumbing and tin shop. The upper left shows lots and dwellings along Dawson and West Central Avenue. Water pipes of 4 to 6 inches are marked. Neighbouring sheets are 10 above, 19 and 17 to the left, 8 and 4 below, 5 to the right.
notes: Dawson is today's Dawson Street.
The railroad is the Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division, called Pemberton Industrial Track in OpenStreetMap; its crossing with North Washington Avenue was rejected by the fit at 2.9 m.
West 3rd Street carries rails near its north end in OpenStreetMap, so the North Washington Avenue and West 3rd Street junction may be slightly displaced.
P.R.R. Amboy Div., West Moorestown station, high school, W. Central Av, N. Church, N. Washington Av, Dawson. 50 ft. Turned.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the north-west side of the centre of Moorestown, around the Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. West 3rd Street and East 3rd Street run down the middle with the railroad beside them, and the two lines cross Mill at about half the height of the sheet. East 2nd and West 2nd Streets run down the right. French Avenue closes the top, North Washington Avenue crosses at the bottom, and Beech runs down the left. The upper left holds a long row of frame dwellings on Beech and the J. S. Collin's & Son Inc. wagon shed and wood working shop, with the Moorestown Ice & Storage Co. Inc. plant and a dairy receiving station beside the railroad. Below Mill, the J. S. Collin's & Son Inc. lumber and coal yard, feed mill, hardware and farm implements store and lumber sheds fill the area west of the line, served by sidings. East of the railroad are dwellings, a junk storage building, a plumbing shop and open lots. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run in the streets. A compass rose is at the lower left. Neighbouring sheets are 20 and 19 to the left, 11 above, 16 and 15 across the left, 6 and 7 to the right and 9 below.
notes: French Av is today's Frenchs Avenue and Dawson St is Dawson Street.
Tippenhauser Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.
The Mill Street and West 3rd Street junction was left out of the fit because the railroad runs in West 3rd Street and put the point 5.6 m off; the rail crossing at the same place is used instead.
Collins lumber yard and ice plant by the railroad, Mill, French Av, Beech, E./W. 3rd (rails in 3rd St; Mill / West 3rd excluded). 50 ft. Turned.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows the block north-east of the railroad in the east part of Moorestown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. Chester Avenue runs across the top of the sheet, with East 3rd Street running down the left-centre beside the Amboy Division of the Pennsylvania Railroad, Plum Street entering from the top and East 2nd Street running down the right-hand side. French Avenue, drawn only 20 feet wide, closes the bottom and Beech Street and Lippincott Avenue lie at the lower left. The row of buildings facing Chester Avenue east of East 3rd Street is mixed commercial and institutional: a Knights of Columbus hall, an auto repair shop, a printing plant with electric power, a small store and the Fire Department of the Relief Engine Co. Beside it the Moorestown Friend's School, marked as to be vacated, stands with its heated, lighted and fire-extinguisher equipped brick buildings. On the other side of Chester Avenue are the 1st Presbyterian Church and a chapel, an auto showroom and repair shop, and a storage warehouse. Below these the sheet is mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings on long narrow lots along the east side of East 3rd Street, and larger scattered houses along East 2nd Street. Much of the ground to the west of the railroad is open or held in large lots. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets. A compass rose appears at the left and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: French Avenue is Frenchs Avenue in OpenStreetMap; East 3rd Street continues south of Chester Avenue as West 3rd Street in OpenStreetMap.
The railroad on the sheet is lettered Amboy Div. P.R.R.
Chester Av, E. 3rd St, Plum St, E. 2nd St, French Av (drawn 20 ft), Beech, Lippincott Av. 50 ft. 4 junctions hand-picked.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the north-east side of Moorestown's centre between East Central Avenue and East 2nd Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper right. Chester Avenue runs down the left side, Newbold Avenue and Chestnut Street run down the middle and right side, and East 3rd Street crosses the sheet as a wide strip with the Amboy Division of the Pennsylvania Railroad beside it. East Central Avenue forms the top edge, with Linden Street entering at the right and Plum Street, Snyder Avenue and East 2nd Street at the bottom. The upper part of the sheet is dwellings, frame and a few stone houses, with outbuildings, set on deep lots between Chester Avenue and Chestnut Street; two large blocks are mostly open ground. At the foot of the Chester Avenue frontage is the E. C. Worrell Engineering Co. with its offices, store and shop. On the railroad stands the Moorestown Passenger Station, with a second track and siding drawn beside the main line. Below the railroad the large block between Chester Avenue and Snyder Avenue is open. Along Plum Street and East 2nd Street are dwellings, a bakery, the New Jersey Bell Telephone Co. Moorestown Exchange, an auto printing and storage building with a capacity of 20 cars, a garage for 12 cars and an auto repair shop, and a small dwelling with a central boiler at the lower right. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and several fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets. A compass rose appears below the railroad and a library stamp and scale bar at the lower right.
notes: Snyder Avenue is lettered with Schooley in parentheses; it is Schooley Street in OpenStreetMap.
East 3rd Street east of Chester Avenue is drawn offset from West 3rd Street west of it (OpenStreetMap has two nodes 14 m apart at Chester Avenue).

E. Central Av, Chester Av, Newbold Av, Chestnut, Linden St, E. 3rd St with the P.R.R. and passenger station, Plum, Snyder Av (Schooley), E. 2nd. 50 ft. Drawn at +27 (90 degrees to sheets 11 and 13). E. 3rd jogs at Chester. Weak fit.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers a residential and light-industrial block of north-eastern Moorestown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. East Central Avenue runs down the left edge, Linden runs down the middle and East 3rd Street runs down the right beside the Pennsylvania Railroad, Amboy Division, while Elm crosses the sheet in the upper third and Chestnut closes the bottom. The upper left block between East Central Avenue and Linden holds scattered frame dwellings with outbuildings on large lots, one with a brick-veneered house, and a compass rose in an open lot. South of Elm the large central block has more dwellings, hot houses and sheds, and a stamp of the Map Division of the Princeton University Library appears at the lower left. East of Linden the lots are narrower: rows of dwellings, a club house, and a large greenhouse with a second greenhouse and a boiler building (marked C.B.). At the bottom right, beside the railroad, stands the plant of E. Hollingshead, dairy, feed and grist mill, with coal bins, hay storage, a storage shed and wood storage, served by a curving siding that leaves the main line. Several small dwellings and barns line Chestnut below. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets, and the right-hand strip of the sheet is taken up by the railroad right of way. The adjoining sheets are numbered 12, 14, 23 and 24 on the margins.
notes: The railroad is lettered P.R.R. (Amboy Div'n).
E. Central Av, Elm, Linden, Chestnut, E. 3rd St, railroad on the east edge. 50 ft.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows the north-eastern edge of the built-up area of Moorestown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. East Central Avenue runs down the left side, Linden down the middle and East 3rd Street down the right beside the Pennsylvania Railroad, Amboy Division, whose main line and a second track fill the right-hand margin. Pearl crosses the sheet near the top and Zeeley Avenue near the bottom, and Stanwick Avenue enters at the top left corner as a diagonal street with lots of irregular shape. Most of the sheet is open or sparsely built: a row of nine matching frame dwellings with outbuildings stands along the east side of Linden between Pearl and Zeeley Avenue, and a few dwellings and barns lie in the blocks above Pearl, on Stanwick Avenue and below Zeeley Avenue, where two houses are marked as having central boilers. The largest building is the contractors' storage of Wm. King beside East 3rd Street, a brick warehouse of one storey with a raised floor section, an office and a storage annex, with its west end marked ruins of fire, no roof, no heat and no lights. A small school building, the Moorestown Public School (Primary), stands in the open block east of Linden, heated and lighted. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets, a compass rose is drawn in the centre of the sheet, and a library stamp and scale bar are at the lower left.
notes: Zeeley Avenue is Zelley Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Stanwick Avenue corresponds to North Stanwick Road.
The railroad is lettered P.R.R. (Amboy Div'n).
Stanwick Av, Pearl, Zeeley Av (Zelley Avenue), E. Central Av, Linden, E. 3rd St, railroad. 50 ft.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows a residential area on the west side of Moorestown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 83 degrees from the usual orientation so that Fairview Avenue and Collins Avenue run across the page and Kenilworth Avenue and West 3rd Street run up and down it. The sheet is bounded at the left by the Pennsylvania Railroad, Amboy Division, which runs the full height of the sheet just outside the first row of lots, and the plan is divided into four tiers of blocks by Fairview Avenue across the upper third and Collins Avenue along the bottom edge. Kenilworth Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, and West 3rd Street forms the right-hand boundary of the drawn blocks. Almost every building is a frame dwelling marked D, each standing on a deep, narrow lot with a few small outbuildings such as sheds and garages at the rear; the lots are numbered with house numbers in the 300s and 400s along the avenues. A small number of buildings are shaded blue or pink, and two fire alarm boxes, one at the upper right and one at the corner of West 3rd Street, are marked. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes are drawn in the middle of Kenilworth, West 3rd and Collins, with the street width of 50 feet written on the pipes. The blank strip at the top and the large unbuilt tracts at the top left and top right are lots without buildings. Block numbers 62, 165, 166 and 167 are printed in the lot groups, with sheet numbers 15, 16, 8 and 21 at the margins to show the adjoining sheets.
notes: The sheet is turned so that north is roughly to the lower left; the fitted rotation is about -83 degrees.
Sheet numbers printed at the edges of the sheet: 16 (left and top), 8 (top), 21 (right).
Fairview Av, Kenilworth Av, Collins Av, W. 3rd St. 50 ft. Turned (north to the left). 4 junctions only.

sheet-16-1.description: The main part of sheet 16 covers the north-west edge of Moorestown where Locust Street and Cedar Street cross the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points towards the upper left. North Church Street runs down the right-hand edge; Locust Street crosses the top of the sheet from North Church Street to its bend at Park Boulevard and then runs diagonally down to the railroad, and Cedar Street runs from North Church Street to the tracks and on to the north-west. West Central Avenue runs parallel to the railroad on its south-west side, and West Maple Avenue and Walker Avenue meet North Church Street at the right edge. The double track of the railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the bottom. The blocks between Locust Street, Cedar Street and North Church Street hold frame dwellings with automobile houses on deep lots and, in block 64, the brick Public School No. 7 (Colored) with a lunch room and gymnasium in the basement. Further dwellings, a cooper's shop and sheds line Cedar Street and North Church Street in block 63. West of the railroad the sheet is thinly built: a few dwellings along Locust Street and a large frame shed in block 166. The lower left corner is taken up by an inset of the Moorestown Water Works, treated as a separate part.
notes: The railroad is lettered R.R. (Amboy Div'n); OpenStreetMap names the line Pemberton Industrial Track.
Locust and West Maple Avenue meet North Church Street at nearly the same point; today Locust Street continues as West Maple Avenue across North Church Street.
The drawn junction of Locust and Park Boulevard lies about 11 m from the modern node and was not used.

Locust, Cedar, N. Church St, W. Central Av, Pennsylvania RR crossing. 50 ft. Part 2: boxed inset at bottom left, Moorestown Water Works pumping station on King's Highway (Haddonfield Av) at the North Branch Pennsauken Creek, own north arrow.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Moorestown Water Works pumping station on King's Highway (Haddonfield Av) at the North Branch Pennsauken Creek (no street junction; the neighbouring printed sheet 27 is not in the manifest; needs step 6b from printed sheet 27, which is not in this manifest; a scan of it is in the separate lenola-1929 atlas (another catalog record), or the creek crossing of Kings Highway from hydrography).

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the north-western edge of Moorestown between North Church Street and Irving Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. North Church Street runs along the bottom, West Central Avenue down the right-hand edge and Dawson across the middle; Walker Avenue climbs from North Church Street at the lower left, and the broad diagonal of Irving Street runs from the upper left to meet Dawson. At the top left, West Oak Avenue branches north-eastward and Irving Court ends in a turning circle. The north-west corner is a newly subdivided tract with several houses and many marked foundations of buildings not yet erected. A row of ten frame dwellings, one with a cinder block outbuilding, fronts the south side of Dawson, with further dwellings at the right corner. A narrow strip of water, drawn in blue, runs between two lots west of the row. Large parts of the middle of the sheet are open ground divided into numbered blocks (59, 168, 169, 192), and the left edge adjoins sheet 22. The lower strip along North Church Street is the most built-up: two rows of frame dwellings with outbuildings, a hall, and a pair of semi-detached houses coloured as brick, on narrow lots running back from the street. Walker Avenue carries a handful of houses on its west side. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets, with a compass rose at the top centre, a library stamp at the lower left and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Irving Street is Irving Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the modern line runs about 6 m to one side of the drawn street.
Dawson is Dawson Street in OpenStreetMap.
N. Church, W. Central Av, Dawson, Walker Av, Irving St and Ct (modern Irving Avenue about 6 m off the drawn street), W. Oak Av. 50 ft. 4 points, 2 hand-picked.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows a residential area on the north-west side of Moorestown around the crossing of North Washington Avenue with West Maple Avenue and West Oak Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned slightly so that north points up and to the right. North Washington Avenue runs the full height of the sheet slightly left of centre, West Maple Avenue crosses it near the upper middle and West Oak Avenue near the foot, and Mill runs down the right-hand edge with East Maple Avenue and East Oak Avenue lettered where it meets them. At the left, Maple Terrace is drawn 40 feet wide, ends in a turning circle and is marked not opened. At the lower left corner Irving Street curves off the sheet. The blocks between West Maple Avenue and West Oak Avenue are filled with frame dwellings and outbuildings: a row of nine on the south side of West Maple Avenue and another row of eight beside West Oak Avenue on the left, and a row of five and a looser group on the right between North Washington Avenue and Mill. North of West Maple Avenue, a new development along both sides of North Washington Avenue has several dwellings with a string of lots on the right marked only with foundations of unbuilt houses; the ground between Maple Terrace and North Washington Avenue and the large block 66 beyond remain open. Lot numbers and block numbers are printed, with water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches marked in the streets. A compass rose stands at the upper right, a library stamp and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Maple Terrace is marked not opened and does not appear in OpenStreetMap.
Mill is Mill Street in OpenStreetMap.
N. Washington Av, W. Maple Av, W. Oak Av, Mill, Maple Ter (not opened). 50 ft. 4 junctions only.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the north-western part of Moorestown around the crossings of Mill, West Central Avenue and North Washington Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. East Oak Avenue and West Oak Avenue meet Mill at the left edge, Mill crosses the sheet from left to right at about one third of its height, and E. Central Avenue and W. Central Avenue run down the middle. North Washington Avenue crosses below Mill and W. Central Avenue turns south-east at the foot of the sheet toward Dawson, while Beech enters from the upper right and Irving appears at the bottom. The blocks bounded by these streets are mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings on large lots, many with brick or coloured fronts, with an open lot at the left centre and block 170 at the lower left shown unbuilt except for foundations marked A and B. The 2nd Baptist Church (Colored), heated by steam and lit by electricity, stands in the upper right block next to Mill. A creek, drawn in blue, runs from the top of the sheet down the right-hand side past the Moorestown Steam Laundry, a group of brick and frame buildings with a concrete floor, a water tank and an R.R. siding, with no watchman, heat and power by steam, lights electric and fuel coal, with fire buckets and extinguishers. The creek then turns south-west across Central Avenue to the foot of the sheet. Rows of dwellings line both sides of W. Central Avenue as it bends toward Dawson, and several houses stand on Dawson at the lower right. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets, with a compass rose near the middle and a library stamp and scale bar at the bottom left.
notes: Mill, Dawson and Beech are Mill Street, Dawson Street and Beech Street in OpenStreetMap.
E./W. Oak Av, Mill, E./W. Central Av, N. Washington Av, Dawson, Irving, Beech, creek. 50 ft.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows a residential district in the north of Moorestown between Chester Avenue and Beech, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. Chester Avenue forms the top edge, E. Oak Avenue runs down the left side, E. Central Avenue down the middle, and Lippincott Avenue crosses the sheet at about two thirds of its height. Beech runs down the lower right, slanting to the right, and the section of Lippincott Avenue east of E. Central Avenue is lettered not open. The sheet is almost entirely frame dwellings with outbuildings: large houses of two and three storeys with brick-veneered fronts and wings at the upper left, between Chester Avenue and Lippincott Avenue, on deep lots, and rows of smaller dwellings along the south side of Lippincott Avenue and along the east side of E. Central Avenue. A stone dwelling with an open porch stands on E. Oak Avenue and one house is noted with a frame attic. East of E. Central Avenue the lots north of Lippincott Avenue are long strips running to the right edge, built up only at their near ends, and on the south side of Lippincott Avenue the blocks below it are numbered 26 and 29. A compass rose lies at the upper right, with a library stamp and the scale bar at the bottom. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in the streets, and sheet and block numbers (2, 23, 26, 29) are printed within the blocks. The adjoining sheets are 11, 12, 19 and 23.
notes: Beech is Beech Street in OpenStreetMap.
Lippincott Avenue east of East Central Avenue is lettered Not Open.
Chester Av, E. Oak Av, E. Central Av, Lippincott Av (not open east of E. Central), Beech. 50 ft.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the western edge of Moorestown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points roughly to the left of the page (fitted rotation about -75 degrees). The long diagonal of Camden Avenue runs up the left-centre of the sheet, with West 3rd Street along the left margin, Mannion Avenue and Fairview Avenue crossing from the west, and Collins Avenue below, where the sheet adjoins sheet 15 on the left. The line of King's Highway, also lettered as Haddonfield Avenue, crosses the centre of the sheet from top to bottom and is crossed by Colonial Avenue, Highland Avenue and Pleasant Valley Road. Crescent Avenue curves down the right-hand side past Pembrook Avenue and Highland Avenue to the developed streets of the lower right, where Valley View Terrace, Stratford-Lakeview Drive, Lincoln Terrace and Stoke's Terrace enclose a block of small frame dwellings on narrow lots. The upper left holds a florist's range of greenhouses labelled H. Otter, Florist, with its dwellings and outbuildings, and an auto repair shop and show room at the top near West Main Street. Most of the sheet is open ground, large undivided parcels with an occasional frame dwelling, and block numbers 69 to 73, 90, 174 to 184 are printed in them. Six-, eight- and ten-inch water pipes are drawn in the streets and a fire alarm box stands at the Pleasant Valley Road crossing of King's Highway. The sheet carries a compass rose at the top left, and a scale of 100 feet to an inch with the Sanborn copyright note at the foot.
notes: Pleasant Valley Road is today's Pleasant Valley Avenue; Stratford-Lakeview Drive is today's Lakeview Drive (with Stratford Drive); Stoke's Terrace is today's Stokes Terrace; King's Highway is today's Kings Highway (East Kings Highway at the top of the sheet).
West 2nd Street changes name to Camden Avenue at Fairview Avenue on the sheet; the modern Camden Avenue / West 2nd Street junction was left out of the fit.
Highland Avenue / Kings Highway was rejected at 8.7 m by the fit and Crescent Avenue / Highland Avenue was not detected.
West end: Camden Av, W. Main, Mannion, Fairview, Collins, King's Highway, Crescent, Highland, Stoke's Ter, Lincoln Ter, Pleasant Valley Rd. 100 ft. Turned.

sheet-22-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 22 is the upper and larger part of the sheet, covering the north-western edge of Moorestown along North Church Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. North Church Street runs down the sheet a third of the way in from the left. West of it are Clark Avenue and Roberts Avenue (Pancoast), short streets with a few dwellings, and Park Boulevard running diagonally to Locust at the lower left; Bethel A.M.E. Church stands on the west side of North Church Street in block 65. East of North Church Street, Bridge leads to Bethel Avenue, along which lie Home Terrace and Coleman, a small grid of house lots in blocks 159, 162 and 166 with scattered frame dwellings. West Maple Avenue leaves North Church Street opposite Locust and runs east across the sheet, crossed by Dawson; a row of dwellings faces North Church Street south of West Maple Avenue, and block 192 (59) is laid out in narrow lots that are still largely empty. At the lower right a few dwellings stand around the turning circle of Irving Court. Much of the sheet, including blocks 154, 155, 158, 161 and 168, is open land with only a handful of buildings. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches run in North Church Street, Locust and West Maple Avenue. A heavy line across the sheet separates this part from part 2, which shows Camden Avenue.
notes: Roberts Av. is also lettered Pancoast.
Coleman is Coleman Terrace and Bridge is Bridge Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The drawn junction of Locust and Park Boulevard does not match the modern node (about 11 m off on sheet 16 as well) and was excluded.
Home Terrace is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line: part 1 (top) N. Church St, Park Blvd, Clark Av, Bethel Av, Bridge, W. Maple Av, Dawson; part 2 (bottom, north up) Camden Av, B Av, Colonial Ridge, Flynn Av.

sheet-22-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 22 is the lower strip of the sheet, below a heavy dividing line, showing a small development on the north side of Camden Avenue at the western edge of Moorestown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north straight up. Camden Avenue runs across the bottom of the part. Colonial Ridge, a 70-foot street with rounded corners, runs north from Camden Avenue and is crossed by B Avenue; Flynn Avenue, 20 feet wide, runs north from Camden Avenue at the right. The blocks along Colonial Ridge (150, 151, 152 and 153) hold a group of brick and frame dwellings with garages, several of them recently built in brick or tile, and further frame dwellings and a hardware shed stand along Camden Avenue towards Flynn Avenue. The rest of the area is open land marked No Exposure along the edges. A 6 inch water pipe runs in Colonial Ridge and an 8 inch pipe in Camden Avenue.
notes: B Avenue is Bowling Green in OpenStreetMap; Colonial Ridge is Colonial Ridge and North Colonial Ridge.
Placed from three hand-picked junctions only (the detector found no junction here); scale and rotation are poorly fixed.

100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line: part 1 (top) N. Church St, Park Blvd, Clark Av, Bethel Av, Bridge, W. Maple Av, Dawson; part 2 (bottom, north up) Camden Av, B Av, Colonial Ridge, Flynn Av.

sheet-23-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 23 covers the residential north-east of Moorestown between Chester Avenue and Elm Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper left. East Maple Avenue, East Oak Avenue and East Central Avenue run down the sheet; Elm crosses near the top, Chestnut about two thirds of the way down, and Chester Avenue runs along the bottom edge, with only its near side drawn. The blocks between the avenues (21, 20, 36, 37, 38 and 80) are divided into regular house lots carrying frame dwellings with automobile houses, a few of brick or stone, and a Private Alley runs behind the lots near Chester Avenue. The lower left corner of the part is taken by the grounds of the Moorestown Field Club, with its club house, caddie house and golf links, and by block 31 with a few dwellings; the ground beyond is marked No Exposure. Blocks 79 and 81 between East Maple and East Oak Avenues north of Chestnut are nearly empty. The upper left of the sheet, inside a heavy line, is a separately oriented inset (part 2) showing Chester Avenue to Mill Street. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches run in the streets and fire alarm boxes are marked at several corners.
notes: Elm is drawn with a jog at East Maple Avenue; that junction disagrees with the modern node by about 12 m and was rejected by the fit.
Chester Avenue along the bottom edge has only its near side drawn.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (right and bottom) E. Maple, E. Oak, E. Central Av, Elm, Chestnut, Chester Av, Moorestown Field Club; part 2 (top left, boxed, north to the left) Chester Av, Lippincott Av, E. Maple, E. Oak, Mill, Flora Croft Gardens.

sheet-23-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 23 is a tall inset in the upper left corner of the sheet, inside a heavy line, showing the strip between East Maple Avenue and East Oak Avenue from Chester Avenue to Mill, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the left as its own arrow shows. It lies south-west of the main part of the sheet, beyond Chester Avenue. Chester Avenue crosses the top of the inset and Mill the bottom, with Lippincott Avenue between them; East Maple Avenue runs down its left side and East Oak Avenue down its right, becoming West Oak Avenue at Mill. Block 22, between Chester and Lippincott Avenues, is mostly taken by the Flora Craft Gardens, a large group of greenhouses with a potting house, boiler house and further greenhouse ranges, together with two dwellings. Block 24, between Lippincott Avenue and Mill, is divided into house lots with frame dwellings facing East Oak Avenue and a brick dwelling on East Maple Avenue. West of East Maple Avenue a few dwellings are drawn with their distances from the street, and in the lower left corner the caddie house of the Moorestown Field Club appears beside an area marked No Exposure. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in Chester Avenue and East Maple Avenue.
notes: The inset is drawn in the corner of sheet 23 but lies south-west of the main part, across Chester Avenue.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (right and bottom) E. Maple, E. Oak, E. Central Av, Elm, Chestnut, Chester Av, Moorestown Field Club; part 2 (top left, boxed, north to the left) Chester Av, Lippincott Av, E. Maple, E. Oak, Mill, Flora Croft Gardens.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the east end of Moorestown along East Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points roughly to the left and slightly down the page (fitted rotation about -68 degrees). East Main runs down the right-centre of the sheet from Zeeley Avenue at the top to Schooley Street at the foot, with Peditts Lane (marked as the old Mt. Laurel Road) and Allens Lane crossing it near the top and Mt. Laurel Road leaving it to the right below the middle. The Pennsylvania Railroad, Amboy Division, runs the full height of the left margin beside East 3rd Street, and Chestnut Street crosses the sheet below the middle from East 3rd Street through East 2nd Street to East Main. Along Chestnut and in the corner of Snyder Avenue, Plum Street, Schooley Street and Bourne Terrace the sheet is closely built with frame dwellings on narrow lots, among them a paint shop and a small group of houses lettered as dwellings with outbuildings. The rest of the sheet, from Zeeley Avenue down the right side of East Main, is large open parcels and farm-like holdings with scattered dwellings and greenhouses, a stone house, and two fire alarm boxes on East Main. Water pipes of four to ten inches are drawn in East Main, East 3rd, East 2nd, Zeeley Avenue and Chestnut Street, and the street widths of 40 to 60 feet are marked. A compass rose stands at the upper left. Block numbers 12, 13, 14, 19, 25, 34, 39 and 51 are printed on the sheet, and the adjoining sheet numbers 12, 13, 14, 7 and 25 appear at its margins.
notes: Zeeley Avenue is Zelley Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Bourne Terrace is today's Eastbourne Terrace; Snyder Avenue is today's Snyder Place; Peditts Lane and Allens Lane are not in OpenStreetMap under those names (Peditts Lane may be today's Featherbed Lane).
The Pennsylvania Railroad, Amboy Division (Pemberton Industrial Track in OpenStreetMap) runs along the left margin of the sheet.
East 3rd Street is drawn on both sides of the railroad at the top of the sheet; the two modern East 3rd Street / Zelley Avenue nodes about 40 m apart both match drawn crossings.
East end: E. Main, Chestnut, E. 2nd and 3rd, Zeeley Av, Bourne Ter, Allens Lane, Peditts Lane (Old Mt. Laurel Rd), Mt. Laurel Rd, P.R.R. 100 ft. Turned.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the eastern residential district of Moorestown north of Zeeley Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points about to the left of the page (fitted rotation about -64 degrees). East 3rd Street, East 2nd Street and East Main run up and down the sheet in parallel, crossed by Stanwick Avenue near the middle, Poplar Avenue in the upper third and Cameron's Lane and Tiver Avenue above it, with Zeeley Avenue and Peditt's Lane (old Mt. Laurel Road) crossing along the foot. The Pennsylvania Railroad, Amboy Division, runs the full height of the sheet between two stretches of East 3rd Street, and a passenger station and a freight siding appear at the Stanwick Avenue crossing. The blocks between the railroad and East Main are closely built with frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with numbered house fronts in the 300s, 400s and 500s, and dwellings with outbuildings continue along East Main and the blocks to its east, together with an auto painting and top rebuilding shop and a furniture upholstery shop. On the left of the sheet beyond the railroad the Moorestown Supply Co. coal yard is drawn with its contractor's storage building, coal sheds and coal pockets, and a small row of dwellings stands on East 4th Street. Near the foot of the sheet two tanks of the Moorestown Water Co. are marked on East Main Street. Madison Avenue runs along the right margin beside block 51, and a stretch of open land to its right holds a few outbuildings. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are marked in the streets. A compass rose is at the upper left.
notes: Zeeley Avenue is Zelley Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Stanwick Avenue is today's North Stanwick Road and South Stanwick Road; Peditt's Lane may be today's Featherbed Lane; Cameron's Lane is not in OpenStreetMap under that name.

East 3rd Street is drawn on both sides of the Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division); the two modern East 3rd Street nodes about 40 m apart at Zelley Avenue and at Stanwick Road both match drawn crossings.

Fitted at about 3.97 px per foot, matching a scale of 100 feet to an inch; the fit has a residual of 2.5 m, higher than other sheets, and the East Main Street / South Stanwick Road junction was rejected at 8.5 m.
East end: E. 2nd, 3rd and 4th, E. Main, Stanwick Av, Poplar Av, Zeeley Av, Tiver Av, Cameron's Lane. 100 ft. Turned. Moderate fit.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the western part of the Lenola district of Moorestown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 30 degrees clockwise so that north points up and to the left of the page (fitted rotation about +30 degrees). Camden Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally from the upper left to Lenola Road on the right, with Cottage Avenue running up from it at the left, and Claypool and New Albany Road leaving it to the north. Lenola Road forms the right-hand edge of the sheet. In the lower two thirds a grid of Winthrop Avenue, Lincoln Avenue, Garfield Avenue and Emerson Avenue encloses the blocks numbered 130 to 135 in the Lenola subdivision, laid out in long narrow lots with frame dwellings and outbuildings, a few coops and a garage, concentrated along Garfield Avenue and Lenola Road. Near the middle right a gasoline filling station and a larger group of buildings, shaded pink and blue, stand close to Camden Avenue and Lenola Road. Along the left of the sheet a wide strip of swamp land is divided by the North Branch Pennsauken Creek, which meanders down the sheet and forms the boundary between Chester Township and Moorestown Township. Blocks of swamp-land lots at the bottom are drawn with lot lines but no buildings. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are marked in the streets, with fire hydrants and a fire alarm box at Winthrop and Lenola Road. The compass rose is at the upper left, and the scale bar of 100 feet to an inch and a Map Division stamp are along the foot.
notes: Claypool is today's Claypoole Avenue; Camden Avenue is West Camden Avenue west of Lenola Road; Lincoln Avenue and Garfield Avenue are South Lincoln Avenue and South Garfield Avenue; New Albany Road is West New Albany Road at Camden Avenue.

The drawn Winthrop Avenue at the top and left of the central blocks (a long frontage 50 feet wide) is not Winthrop Avenue today: in OpenStreetMap it appears as Whittier Avenue and Grant Avenue; only the lower Winthrop Avenue keeps the name.
Franklin Avenue / West Camden Avenue was rejected at 9.4 m (drawn with a jog).
Lenola west: Camden Av, Cottage Av, Winthrop Av (modern Whittier / Grant Avenue), Lincoln, Garfield, Emerson Av, Claypool, North Branch Pennsauken Creek. 100 ft. Rotation +30.

sheet-27.description: This sheet, lettered 28 on the map and the 27th canvas of the volume, covers the Lenola district of Moorestown north of Camden Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 30 degrees so that north points up and to the left of the page. Lenola Road runs down the right-hand side, with Pine and Harding Avenue crossing from the west near the top, and Wilson crossing the middle. Between Harding Avenue and Wilson, and below Wilson, a compact grid of Lincoln Avenue and Garfield Avenue encloses the blocks numbered 104 to 111, narrow lots each holding a frame dwelling with outbuildings, several shaded blue. Below the grid the Pennsylvania Railroad, Amboy Division, crosses the sheet diagonally from the creek at the left past the Lenola Passenger Station and a coal pile to Lenola Road, with Moore Street and Merion Street meeting Lenola Road beside it. South of the railroad, Browning, Cottage Avenue and Claypool enclose blocks 112 to 114 of frame dwellings, with a coal and wood yard of R. W. Johnson and a Pentecostal church on the east side near Lenola Road. Camden Avenue appears at the lower left, with swamp land beyond it. The North Branch Pennsauken Creek, forming the boundary of Chester Township and Moorestown Township, curves down the left edge, and a stream drains across the upper part to it. Sewage Disposal Beds and an area marked No Exposure are noted at the upper left and top. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are marked in the streets, and a compass rose stands at the left.
notes: Canvas sheet-27 shows printed Sheet 28; printed Sheet 27 (Lenola south of Camden Avenue) is not in the manifest. A separate scan of printed sheet 27 is in the lenola-1929 atlas (another catalog record).

Pine is today's Pine Street, Claypool is Claypoole Avenue, Wilson is West Wilson Avenue (East Wilson Avenue east of Lenola Road), Lincoln and Garfield are North Lincoln Avenue and North Garfield Avenue.
Junctions on North Lenola Road and Moore Street are included in the fit (residuals 2 to 4 m); with them the sheet agrees with sheet 29 along Lenola Road.
Merion Street is not matched: modern Merion Avenue beside the railroad does not follow the drawn line.

Canvas labelled Sheet 27 shows printed sheet 28 (Lenola north of Camden Av: Pine, Harding Av, Wilson, Lincoln Av, Garfield Av, Lenola Rd, Moore, Browning, Claypool, Cottage Av, P.R.R. Amboy Div., North Branch Pennsauken Creek, sewage disposal beds). 100 ft. Printed sheet 27 (Lenola south of Camden Av, Kings Highway) is not in the manifest. sheet-29-1.description: The main part of sheet 29 covers the north-eastern side of Lenola along Lenola Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Lenola Road runs diagonally down the left of the sheet from the top edge to New Albany Road, which crosses the bottom. East of Lenola Road a small grid of streets is laid out: Wilson along the top, Moore, Errickson and Winstead crossing the sheet, Harvey Avenue and Grand Avenue running between them. Moore Street, Wilson Street, Browning Street and Claypool Street leave Lenola Road to the west, towards sheets 28 and 26. The Pennsylvania Railroad's double track crosses diagonally from Lenola Road to New Albany Road, with Merion running alongside it on the north-east side; the Gospel Tabernacle stands on Merion near Errickson. Blocks 116 to 125 are divided into narrow house lots carrying rows of small frame dwellings, many of them recently built, and the large block 126 between the railroad and New Albany Road is almost empty. Along New Albany Road are the Lenola Public School (first grade) at Lenola Road, the Lenola Union Church, the brick Lenola Public School, and at the lower left the Lenola Volunteer Fire Co. No. 1. A 6 to 12 inch water pipe system runs in the streets. The strip above the heavy line at the top of the sheet is a separate part showing Center Street.
notes: Wilson is East Wilson Avenue and Wilson St. West Wilson Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Moore is Moore Street; Errickson, Winstead and Merion are Errickson, Winstead and Merion Avenue.
Merion Avenue today does not follow the drawn line beside the railroad (residuals of 6 to 16 m); it was left out of the fit.
Harvey Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Canvas sheet-28 of the manifest is a second scan of this sheet; printed sheet 28 is not in the manifest.

Lenola, 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main) Lenola Rd, Wilson, Moore, Harvey Av, Errickson, Grand Av, Winstead, Merion, New Albany Rd, Pennsylvania RR; part 2 (top strip above heavy line) Center St and Lenola Rd.

sheet-29-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 29 is a narrow strip across the top of the sheet, above a heavy dividing line, showing Center Street in the north of Lenola from Lenola Road eastwards, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the upper right. Lenola Road runs down the left edge, with Pine Street leaving it to the west. Center Street crosses the whole strip, lined on both sides by long narrow lots in blocks 102 and 107, most of them still empty; a scattering of small frame dwellings and automobile houses stands along the street, closer together near Lenola Road. The ground beyond the rear lot lines on both sides is marked No Exposure. A 6 inch water pipe runs along Center Street and Lenola Road.
notes: Placed from a single junction (Center Street and North Lenola Road) with the scale of part 1 and the rotation of the drawn Center Street; low confidence.
